subject: Media Literacy
title: Password Managers and Digital Hygiene
description: A quick win: understand Password Managers and Digital Hygiene.

hook.text: The most common password in the world is '123456.' It protects bank accounts, emails, and medical records.

buildup.text: Digital hygiene means basic security practices — strong unique passwords, two-factor authentication, and regular updates.

discovery.text: Password managers generate and store unique passwords for every account, eliminating the weakest link in security.

twist.text: Most data breaches exploit reused passwords. One leaked password unlocks dozens of accounts.

climax.text: Good digital hygiene stops most attacks. Hackers target easy victims first.

punchline.text: A unique password for every account. It's the simplest powerful defense.

quiz.question: Why are reused passwords dangerous?
options: One leaked password gives access to all accounts using it
